statement: Every safety property Calm Frames claims has a mutation that breaks the code guarding it. The kill rate below is killed divided by attempted, rounded down, over the mutations in eval/mutate_gate.py only. It is not a whole-codebase mutation score and it does not stand in for one.
how_a_kill_is_counted: The tests that guard the mutated line are run as whole files. A kill needs at least one named failing test and no collection or compile error, because both of those also exit non-zero and neither is a test catching anything.

negative_control.description: every selection run unmutated before any mutation was applied

survivors.property: cover held through stalls and seeks
survivors.breaks: going to the background stops hiding the picture at once, and waits for the next scheduler tick instead
survivors.survived_because: every test passed with the guard broken (34 ran)
survivors.equivalent: the cover still goes on at once, by a second path. foreground is in the dependency list of the tick effect, and that effect calls tick() itself before setting its interval, so a change of foreground tears the effect down, builds it again and covers synchronously. The picture is hidden in the same commit either way and no test can see a difference. It was checked rather than assumed: coverHarness.test.tsx now has a test that flips foreground and advances no timers at all, and it stays green with this mutation applied and goes red when foreground is also taken out of that dependency list, which is the only way to actually remove the behaviour. Worth knowing that the redundancy is what makes this equivalent: drop foreground from those deps as a tidy-up and the guard on line 318 becomes load bearing again.

survivors.property: fail closed on a map that is unsigned
survivors.breaks: a map with no signature block is read as if it had one
survivors.survived_because: every test passed with the guard broken (22 ran)
survivors.equivalent: the unsigned path is guarded three times over. With the first check gone, a map with no signature block reaches the algorithm check, where asString(undefined) is not 'ed25519', and is refused as 'unsigned' again. Only the diagnostic detail changes, and nothing user facing reads it: useFlashGuard shows rejectionMessage(reason). No test can tell the two apart, and writing one that pins the wording would be testing a log line.
